module.name: Identity Utility
module.description: This module represents identity utility. It implements the meta-axioms from 7232 (multidimensionality, temporality, context dependency, segment logic). It defines identity as self-definition through belonging and differentiation, anchored in social, cultural, and institutional frameworks. It differs from INU (7234) and KNU (7235) as identities generate independent utility functions with specific pains and gains. IDN acts as a bridge between INU and KNU and is central to Awareness (7240) and Willingness (7243).

A1.title: Chapter Context
A1.text: Module code: BCM2_03_IDN. Type: Utility module. Owner: FehrAdvice & Partners AG. Year: 2025. This module represents identity utility and implements meta-axioms from 7232 including multidimensionality, temporality, context dependency, and segment logic. Identity is defined as self-definition through belonging and differentiation, anchored in social, cultural, and institutional frameworks. It differs from individual utility (INU 7234) and collective utility (KNU 7235) as identities generate independent utility functions with specific pains and gains. IDN acts as a bridge between INU and KNU and is central to Awareness (7240) and Willingness (7243).

A2.title: Scope and Application
A2.text: Applies to all identity utility functions in BCM simulations. Representation of identity situations across social roles, cultural affiliations, gender, digital identities, brand identities, collective affiliations, and life phases. Valid for WEIRD and non-WEIRD contexts. Covers time horizons (instant, short-term, medium-term, long-term). Supports segmentation by identity strength, stability, and context dependency. Applicable for intersectional, hybrid, and collective identities. Foundation for scenarios with norm conflicts, identity crises, shocks, and resilience.

A3.title: Objectives and Functions
A3.text: Objectives: Representation of pain and gain structures of identities. Integration of time horizons and discounting. Aggregation of multiple identities with weightings. Capture of complementarity and conflict between identities. Embedding in social, cultural, and institutional contexts. Dynamic modeling of identity journeys (crisis → transition → stabilization). Consideration of norms, legitimacy, and recognition. Representation of resilience, shocks, and uncertainty. Integration of digital and intergenerational identities. Provision of interface to Awareness (7240) and Willingness (7243).

A4.title: Binding Logic Rules (Identity Axioms IDN-A1 to IDN-A70)
A4.text: This section contains the formal axioms that define the binding logic rules for the Identity Utility module. These axioms establish the foundational principles for identity-based utility modeling, including identity definition, multiplicity, autonomy, net utility, temporality, aggregation, sociality, context dependency, awareness, complementarity, conflict, path dependency, journeys, norms, institutionalization, uncertainty, and various extensions covering digital identity, coherence, fragmentation, emotions, resilience, and the coherence principle.

axioms.title: Definition
axioms.description: An identity is the self-definition of a person through belonging (inclusion) and differentiation (difference) within social, cultural, or institutional frameworks.

axioms.title: Multiplicity
axioms.description: Every person carries multiple identities simultaneously, which act as independent utility sources.

axioms.title: Autonomy
axioms.description: Identities generate specific utilities (gains) and costs (pains) that are not derivable from individual utility (INU) or collective utility (KNU).

axioms.title: Net Utility
axioms.description: The net utility of an identity results from belonging, recognition, and role coherence minus exclusion, stigmatization, and role conflicts.

axioms.title: Temporality
axioms.description: Identity utility unfolds across specific time horizons (instant, short-term, medium-term, long-term) and is modulated by temporal discounting.

axioms.title: Aggregation
axioms.description: The total utility of a person results from the aggregation of multiple identities, weighted by relevance (π_j).

axioms.title: Sociality
axioms.description: Identity utility is relational; it emerges in relation to others and cannot be fully determined without social embedding.

axioms.title: Context Dependency
axioms.description: The salience of an identity depends on context; contexts activate different identities with varying strengths.

axioms.title: Motivated Awareness – Adaptive Self-Coherence
axioms.description: Awareness describes the degree to which an identity is cognitively, emotionally, and socially consciously activated. It determines whether and to what extent potential identity utility becomes effective. Awareness is an adaptive self-regulation function that selectively admits or blocks information to maintain coherence and emotional stability of the self-image. Awareness acts as a filter between potential (latent) and action-guiding (salient) identity.

axioms.title: Complementarity and Conflict
axioms.description: Identities can mutually reinforce each other (complementarity) or contradict each other (conflict), thereby increasing or reducing total utility.

axioms.title: Path Dependency
axioms.description: Identity utility is dynamic and depends on previous experiences, decisions, and events. The past shapes current identity situations.

axioms.title: Identity Journey
axioms.description: Identities develop over journeys (building, crisis, transformation, stabilization). Each phase generates different utility effects.

axioms.title: Norms
axioms.description: Norms strengthen or weaken identity utility through conformity or deviation.

axioms.title: Institutionalization
axioms.description: Institutions can stabilize identities (cost reduction) or destabilize them (cost increase).

axioms.title: Uncertainty
axioms.description: Identity utility is sensitive to uncertainty (epistemic, interpersonal, institutional, environmental).

axioms.title: Temporal Integration
axioms.formula: U_IDN^j = Σ (δ_i^j * ω_i^j * U_i^j), i ∈ {instant, short, medium, long}
axioms.description: Identity utility is integrated across all time horizons, from instant to long-term.

axioms.title: Temporal Profiles
axioms.description: Different identities have different temporal profiles (e.g., transient vs. institutional).

axioms.title: Discounting
axioms.description: Identity utility is temporally discounted, with discount rates varying by identity type.

axioms.title: Temporal Dynamics
axioms.description: The weighting of time horizons changes dynamically over life phases.

axioms.title: Temporal Feedback
axioms.description: Short-term identity gains can cause long-term identity costs (and vice versa).

axioms.title: Identity Gains
axioms.description: Identity gains arise from recognition, belonging, coherence, and norm conformity.

axioms.title: Identity Pains
axioms.description: Identity costs arise from exclusion, stigmatization, dissonance, and conflicts.

axioms.title: Asymmetry of Pains and Gains
axioms.description: Identity pains weigh more heavily than identity gains.

axioms.title: Complementary Gains
axioms.formula: G_total = Σ G_i^j + Σ κ_jk^+ * (G^j * G^k)
axioms.description: Different identities can positively complement each other in their gains.

axioms.title: Conflict Costs
axioms.formula: C_total = Σ C_i^j + Σ κ_jk^- * Conflict(j,k)
axioms.description: Conflicts between identities generate additional costs.

axioms.title: Dominance
axioms.description: The dominant identity in a context determines behavioral tendency.

axioms.title: Stability
axioms.description: Identities differ in their temporal stability.

axioms.title: Strength
axioms.description: The strength of an identity depends on salience, emotional intensity, and relevance.

axioms.title: Context Dependency
axioms.description: The activation of identities varies by context.

axioms.title: Relationality
axioms.description: Identity utility also results from differentiation from other identities.

axioms.title: Temporal-Specific Gains
axioms.description: Identity gains can be differentiated by time horizons (instant, short-term, medium-term, long-term).

axioms.title: Temporal-Specific Pains
axioms.description: Identity costs occur at different time horizons and can have temporally different effects.

axioms.title: Time Definitions by Identity Type
axioms.description: Different identity types have different time horizons (transient, institutional, hybrid).

axioms.title: Reversibility
axioms.description: Identity gains can be lost and identity costs can be overcome.

axioms.title: Temporal Feedback
axioms.description: Short-term gains can generate long-term costs, and vice versa.

axioms.title: Autonomous Pains
axioms.description: Identities can generate autonomous pains that operate independently of individual or collective utility.

axioms.title: Autonomous Gains
axioms.description: Identities can generate autonomous gains that cannot be substituted by INU or KNU.

axioms.title: Asymmetric Effect
axioms.description: Identity pains have stronger and longer-lasting effects than identity gains.

axioms.title: Segment-Specific Differences
axioms.description: Identity pains and gains differ by segments (age, gender, culture, role).

axioms.title: Contextual Conflicts
axioms.description: Identity conflicts arise specifically in certain contexts.

axioms.title: Norm Integration
axioms.description: Identity utility is strengthened by coherence with social norms and weakened by norm conflicts.

axioms.title: Interventions
axioms.description: Interventions can influence identity utility through symbols, narratives, and roles.

axioms.title: Identity Journeys
axioms.description: Identities develop over life journeys with characteristic phases and transitions.

axioms.title: Adaptive Identity Uncertainty
axioms.description: Uncertainty describes the degree of instability and ambiguity that a person experiences regarding their identity. It arises from the difference between self-image and social reality and is dynamically influenced by awareness, emotion, self-worth, and context. Identity uncertainty is an adaptive feedback variable that has a stabilizing effect in the short term and a regulatory effect in the long term.

axioms.title: Bridge Function
axioms.description: Identity utility acts as a bridge between individual utility (INU) and collective utility (KNU).

axioms.title: Digital Identity
axioms.formula: U_IDN^digital ≠ U_IDN^physical; U_IDN_total = U_IDN^digital + U_IDN^physical + κ*Interaction
axioms.description: Digital identities generate autonomous pains and gains that interact with physical identities.

axioms.title: Coherence vs. Fragmentation
axioms.description: A fragmented identity architecture increases identity costs.

axioms.title: Intergenerational Identity
axioms.description: Identities are transmitted across generations and generate utility or costs through continuity or breaks.

axioms.title: Macro Level
axioms.description: Social, cultural, and national frameworks shape identity utility.

axioms.title: Resource Binding
axioms.description: Identities require investments of time, money, and energy; these costs reduce net utility.

axioms.title: Conscious vs. Unconscious Identity
axioms.description: Even unconscious identities have an effect, even when awareness = 0.

axioms.title: Shocks and Transformation
axioms.description: External shocks can abruptly destabilize or transform identities.

axioms.title: Intersectionality
axioms.description: Overlaps of multiple identities generate specific pains and gains.

axioms.title: Dynamic Weighting
axioms.description: The relevance weights of identities change dynamically over time and life phases.

axioms.title: Multiplicative Effects
axioms.description: Combinations of identities can generate disproportionate effects.

axioms.title: Collective Identity
axioms.description: Collective identities connect IDN with KNU and generate hybrid utility functions.

axioms.title: Emotional Intensity – Affective Coherence Regulation
axioms.formula: U_IDN_emotional(t) = ψ1 * [A_j(t) - Uncertainty^j(t) + θ*SelfWorth^j(t) + ρ*Resonance^j(t)] * U_IDN^j(t)
axioms.description: Emotional intensity describes the degree to which emotions amplify or dampen identity utility. It acts as an adaptive feedback variable between awareness, uncertainty, and coherence and translates cognitive tensions into affective energy. Emotion is the affective regulator of identity, translating tensions into energy, controlling awareness, modulating uncertainty, and defining the stability of the self over time and context.

axioms.title: Identity Investment
axioms.description: People consciously invest resources in identities; these investments generate returns or losses.

axioms.title: Legitimacy and Recognition
axioms.description: The full utility of an identity depends on its social legitimacy.

axioms.title: External Awareness
axioms.description: The utility of an identity also arises from the effect of one's own behavior on the identities of others.

axioms.title: Parallel Journeys
axioms.description: Multiple identity journeys can run simultaneously (e.g., professional and family). Their interplay influences total utility.

axioms.title: Reversibility of Pains and Gains
axioms.description: Identity costs can be overcome, and identity gains can be lost.

axioms.title: Neutrality
axioms.description: Identities can be inactive and generate neither gains nor pains in a context.

axioms.title: Hierarchy of Conflicts
axioms.description: Not all identity conflicts are equally severe; dominant conflicts override weaker ones.

axioms.title: Identity Mobility
axioms.description: Identities differ in how easily they can be changed or transformed.

axioms.title: Global vs. Local Norms
axioms.description: Identity utility is influenced differently by global (universal) and local (cultural, milieu-specific) norms.

axioms.title: Resilience
axioms.description: Identities have different resistance to external shocks.

axioms.title: Measurability of Returns
axioms.description: Investments in identities can be measured by identity-related returns.

axioms.title: Meta-Relationality
axioms.description: Identity utility emerges from the balance between self-definition and external attribution.

axioms.title: Coherence Principle – Adaptive Integration Performance of Identity
axioms.description: Coherence describes the ability of an identity to maintain an experienced unity of self despite internal and social tensions. It emerges from the interaction of awareness, emotion, uncertainty, self-worth, and social context. Coherence is the integrative mechanism of identity utility. It maintains the balance between awareness, emotion, and uncertainty and thereby enables psychological and social stability. Coherence is the balance of identity between perceiving, feeling, and persisting.

A5.title: Prerequisites and Requirements
A5.text: Data on identity pains and gains (e.g., recognition, exclusion, belonging, stigma). Segment parameters: role, culture, gender, age, institutions. Intersectional identity situations. Temporal parameters and discount factors. Awareness levels. Norms and legitimacy indicators. Context parameters (situations, milieus). Resilience and shock data. Digital identity parameters (privacy, reputation, connectivity, avatar). Resource investments in identities.

A6.title: Module Integration and Linkages
A6.text: Meta modules: 7232 META, 9232 STD. Awareness and Willingness: 7240 AWX, 7243 WAX. Utility modules: 7234 INU, 7235 KNU. Context and Segment: 8904 KON, 7257 SEG. Journey and Life Phases: 7256 JNY, 7457 LCP. Uncertainty and Complexity: 9485–9494. Intervention and Monitoring: 9250 INT, 9251 WATCHDOG. Extended Logics: 9477 STA, 9479 SPT, 9480 GAM.

A7.title: Semantic Boundaries and Limitations
A7.text: The module exclusively represents identity utility. Individual utility INU (7234) and collective utility KNU (7235) remain independent. External frameworks only insofar as they affect identity utility. Aggregation of IDN with INU and KNU occurs only through architecture standards. The module itself does not generate interventions but provides input for 9250 (INT).

A8.title: Version Control and Registry
A8.text: Version history: v1.0 – Basic structure, differentiation from INU/KNU. v1.1 – Structural conformity according to 9232 (A1–A10). v2.0 – Extension with time horizons, awareness, context. v2.1 – Introduction of complementarity and conflicts. v2.2 – Integration of norms, institutions, legitimacy. v2.3 – Extension with digital identity. v2.4 – Incorporation of resilience, shocks, uncertainty. v2.5 – Investment and ROI of identities. v3.0 – Complete integration A1–A70, including coherence principle.
